topStories.headline: New Nonprofit Cinema 'The Portal' Coming to Bernal Heights This Fall
topStories.dek: A 49-seat arthouse cinema is under construction on Mission Street, poised to become San Francisco's first new movie theater in over a decade.
topStories.body:
A new chapter in San Francisco cinema is taking shape at 3293 Mission Street, where The Portal Cinema — a nonprofit, single-screen, 49-seat theater — is under construction and scheduled to open this fall. <cite index="26-2,26-3">The theater will be located in the Mission District neighborhood and will showcase new global releases, repertory works, special programs, and more, equipped to screen archive-only 35mm and 16mm prints, along with digital formats.</cite>

<cite index="26-4">The Portal Cinema marks the first new movie theater built in San Francisco in more than a decade, according to its backers.</cite> <cite index="25-9">The programming will be an eclectic mix of new arthouse and repertory cinema, according to founder and programmer Nellie Killian.</cite>

<cite index="28-2,28-3">Killian settled on 3293 Mission Street, a former real estate office that she leased three years ago, and has since been fundraising, designing and constructing the movie house, with design handled by Atkinson Architecture.</cite>

<cite index="26-5,26-6">A crowdfunding campaign has launched on Kickstarter to ensure the Portal's opening, with a goal of raising $250,000 to fund an electrical panel upgrade, 35mm projection, and a 5.1 sound system so it can open at full capacity this fall.</cite> The theater's website confirms an October 2026 opening target.

topStories.headline: Mission Street Vendor Crackdown Yields 396 Warnings, Zero Arrests After Two Months
topStories.dek: New state law SB 276, targeting unpermitted sellers of suspected stolen goods, is showing early results on Mission Street sidewalks — though enforcement gaps remain after dark.
topStories.body:
<cite index="35-3">City officials, vendors, and businesses in San Francisco's Mission District are reporting cleaner sidewalks and fewer unpermitted sellers offering suspected stolen merchandise since the implementation of a new state bill in June.</cite>

<cite index="35-7">The new bill, SB 276, authored by state Senator Scott Wiener and San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie specifically for San Francisco last year, allows enforcement against people selling commonly stolen goods without a permit or proof of purchase.</cite> <cite index="38-15,38-16">According to city data, in the two months since the law's implementation, the San Francisco Police Department has issued 396 warnings, 46 first-time citations and six second-time citations, with no misdemeanor arrests made.</cite>

<cite index="38-7,38-8,38-9,38-10,38-11">Rodrigo Lopez, president of the Mission Street Vendors Association, said the city has made significant progress: "Everything is under control. Not 100%. And we don't expect it to be 100%. So right now, at this point, the city has control over that issue."</cite> <cite index="38-12">Lopez said the neighborhood's 33 permitted vendors are now operating in designated locations.</cite>

<cite index="36-17,36-18">Despite the reported progress, police acknowledged ongoing challenges during nighttime hours due to staffing limitations, with Officer Rueca noting enforcement remains constrained by available personnel.</cite>

topStories.headline: Mission District Organizations Rally to Support Immigrant Families as School Year Begins
topStories.dek: As students return to classrooms, a network of nonprofits along the Mission corridor is providing legal aid, housing resources, and school-readiness support to immigrant families navigating an uncertain climate.
topStories.body:
<cite index="71-1,71-2">As immigrant students return to school after summer break, a network of organizations is helping support the families with legal aid, housing resources, and more.</cite> The Mission District's dense concentration of immigrant-serving nonprofits has made the neighborhood a hub for this kind of multi-pronged back-to-school outreach.

<cite index="72-4,72-5,72-6">Organizations like Mission Action, located at 938 Valencia Street, connect Latinx, low-income immigrants, and mixed-status families to vital resources like legal aid and housing support, with a mission to build a more informed and empowered society through education and mobilization.</cite>

<cite index="72-15,72-16,72-17">La Raza Centro Legal provides trusted legal aid for low-income, immigrant and Spanish-speaking communities, including immigration clinics held on the second and fourth Thursdays of each month, with legal assistance for citizenship, green card renewals, family petitions, and deportation defense.</cite>

The renewed focus on family support comes against the backdrop of ongoing federal immigration enforcement pressure. <cite index="74-1,74-2,74-3">The San Francisco Immigrant Legal Education Network (SFILEN) has provided training to Mission Housing Resident Services staff on the Rapid Response Network, and Mission Housing staffers are conducting Know Your Rights educational forums in community rooms, open to anyone who wants to help protect the rights of San Franciscans.</cite>

events.title: SF Queer Film Festival (SFQFF26) at the Roxie
events.description: <cite index="106-3">The SF Queer Film Festival's 2026 program runs through the week at the Roxie, with screenings including SFQFF26: Cafe International, Men's Shorts, Velvet Vision, Smash the Cis-tem, Surviving Voices, and more.</cite>

events.title: Bernal Village Marketplace Pop-Up
events.description: <cite index="123-5">This unique indoor pop-up features 10–12 rotating, carefully curated vendors — from clothing designers and ceramicists to bakers, jewelers, vintage curators, graphic artists, soap and candle makers, and organic pet food chefs.</cite> Free admission, family- and pet-friendly.

events.title: Heights Mercantile Farmers Market
events.description: <cite index="126-1,126-2">Join the bimonthly market for fresh produce, meat, cheese, kombucha, flowers, and live music; held the second and fourth Sunday of every month, rain or shine.</cite>

events.title: Bernal Village Marketplace Pop-Up
events.description: <cite index="124-1">The Bernal Village Marketplace returns for its final August installment on August 30, offering local makers and artisans in a community-oriented setting on Cortland Avenue.</cite> Free admission.

events.title: CMC Jazz Night at The Halfway Club
events.location: The Halfway Club, 1166 Geneva Ave, Outer Mission
events.description: <cite index="18-3,18-4,18-5">Join the San Francisco Community Music Center for a jazz night featuring performances by CMC's Advanced Jazz Ensemble led by Patrick Greene, along with additional local musicians — with food, drinks, and an open jam.</cite>

events.title: Fiesta on the Hill
events.description: <cite index="55-1,55-2,55-3,55-4">Fiesta on the Hill is the Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center's biggest fundraiser and a celebration of community, featuring face painting, arts and crafts, community resources, and more, on September 20, 2026, 10am–4pm.</cite>

moreNews.headline: Nightlife Venue 'Downtime' to Transform Former Bissap Baobab Space on Mission Street
moreNews.body: <cite index="7-3,7-4">The Mission District is set to welcome a major new nightlife concept, with Downtime scheduled to open in 2026 at 2243 Mission Street, envisioning a 6,000-square-foot venue that blends dining, cocktails, and a dance floor under one roof.</cite> <cite index="7-5">The space formerly housed Bissap Baobab, a beloved Mission institution that closed at the end of 2025.</cite> <cite index="7-6">The restaurant component will be led by Rose Pizzeria's team from Berkeley, with Eric Ochoa of Dalva designing the cocktail program and a custom sound system gearing the venue toward music-forward performances.</cite>

moreNews.headline: Bernal Heights Playground Reopens After Accessible Renovation
moreNews.body: <cite index="9-1">The San Francisco Recreation and Park Department celebrated the reopening of the Bernal Heights Playground, unveiling a refreshed and fully accessible play space in a project where construction began in August 2025 and was completed in record time thanks to the city's new cooperative purchasing framework.</cite> <cite index="9-5">Guided by community input, the project reflects neighborhood priorities while meeting modern ADA accessibility standards.</cite>

restaurants.name: Foreign Cinema
restaurants.description: Iconic Mission institution where films are projected on the back courtyard wall while diners enjoy California-Mediterranean cuisine; a consistent Chronicle Top 100 pick since 1999.

restaurants.name: Flour + Water
restaurants.description: Beloved Mission pasta destination known for Neapolitan wood-fired pizza and creative rotating pasta tasting menus using Northern California ingredients.

restaurants.name: Tartine Bakery
restaurants.description: World-renowned Mission bakery famous for its country loaf, morning buns, and pastries from Chad Robertson and Elisabeth Prueitt.

restaurants.name: Dandelion Chocolate
restaurants.description: Mission's celebrated bean-to-bar chocolate factory and café offering single-origin drinking chocolate, pastries, and confections made on-site.

restaurants.name: Bi-Rite Creamery
restaurants.description: The Mission's much-loved scoop shop, famous for salted caramel ice cream and seasonal, locally sourced flavors with a perpetual line out the door.

restaurants.name: Taqueria El Farolito
restaurants.description: A late-night Mission institution and consistent Infatuation top pick for super burritos, tacos al pastor, and no-frills authentic Mexican street food.

restaurants.name: La Taqueria
restaurants.description: James Beard Award–winning Mission taqueria celebrated for its no-rice burritos and carne asada tacos, a neighborhood anchor for over four decades.

restaurants.name: Loló
restaurants.description: Jaliscan-Californian inspired restaurant known for inventive cocktails, creative tacos, and colorful patio dining on Valencia Street.

restaurants.name: Lolinda
restaurants.description: Upscale Argentine steakhouse on Valencia Street featuring wood-fired meats and a rooftop bar (El Techo) with panoramic city views.

restaurants.name: San Ho Won
restaurants.description: Mission's top-rated Korean barbecue destination with a lychee-wood charcoal grill, creative banchan, and an Infatuation 9.5 rating.

restaurants.name: Rintaro
restaurants.description: Acclaimed Japanese izakaya in a handcrafted cedar space, offering yakitori, handmade soba, and seasonal Japanese dishes.

restaurants.name: Delfina Restaurant
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Italian trattoria beloved for rustic pasta, wood-fired dishes, and a warm atmosphere that has anchored the 18th Street dining strip for decades.

restaurants.name: Pancho Villa Taqueria
restaurants.description: High-volume Mission taqueria on 16th Street known for generous burritos and quick, affordable Mexican staples.

restaurants.name: Taqueria Cancún
restaurants.description: A Mission staple for super burritos and tacos, praised by The Infatuation for its excellent execution of classic Mission-style Mexican food.

restaurants.name: Al Carajo
restaurants.description: Chef-owner Javier Leon's Yucateco spot on 22nd Street, celebrated for cochinita pibil tacos, recado negro al pastor, and salbutes.

restaurants.name: Mijoté
restaurants.description: Intimate French bistro on Valencia earning consistent top ratings from The Infatuation for its classic bistro fare and warm neighborhood feel.

restaurants.name: Limon Rotisserie
restaurants.description: Bright Mission restaurant known for Peruvian-inspired rotisserie chicken, ceviche, and pisco cocktails in a lively space.

restaurants.name: Sightglass Coffee
restaurants.description: Popular specialty coffee roaster with a Mission outpost offering expertly sourced single-origin coffees and espresso drinks in a bright café space.

restaurants.name: Ritual Coffee Roasters
restaurants.description: Mission flagship of SF's beloved third-wave roaster, with the roaster visible in the back of the café so guests can watch their beans being processed.

restaurants.name: St. Francis Fountain
restaurants.type: Old-school American diner and soda fountain
restaurants.description: A Mission institution since 1918, serving classic diner breakfasts, burgers, and egg creams alongside a rotating gallery of local art.

restaurants.name: Humphry Slocombe
restaurants.description: Mission's wildly creative ice cream shop famous for offbeat flavors like Secret Breakfast (bourbon-cornflake), jalapeño, and olive oil.

restaurants.name: Piglet & Co
restaurants.description: Creative, Taiwan-inspired comfort food restaurant in the Mission, an Eater Best New Restaurants pick, with a frequently rotating menu inspired by night markets.

restaurants.name: Emmy's Spaghetti Shack
restaurants.description: Beloved Mission-Bernal neighborhood spot for casual, cozy Italian comfort dishes including pasta and meatballs in a laid-back atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Komaaj
restaurants.description: Acclaimed northern Iranian restaurant on Mission Street, praised for its refined Persian cooking and distinctive rice dishes.

restaurants.name: PizzaHacker
restaurants.description: Neighborhood pizza shop on the Mission-Bernal border renowned for creative, high-quality pies with a devoted local following.

hotels.name: Parker Guest House
hotels.description: A 19-room boutique inn in a pair of Edwardian mansions near the Mission, Castro, and Noe Valley, offering free breakfast, a garden, and an afternoon wine social.

shops.name: Dog Eared Books
shops.description: Long-standing Mission bookstore on Valencia Street carrying new, used, and remaindered titles alongside a strong selection of small-press and local literature.

shops.name: Medicine for Nightmares Bookshop & Gallery
shops.description: A community-rooted bookshop and gallery in the Calle 24 Latino Cultural District specializing in literature and art by and for BIPOC communities.

shops.name: Borderlands Books
shops.description: Beloved Mission bookshop specializing in science fiction, fantasy, mystery, and horror, with an attached café that encourages leisurely browsing.

shops.name: Bi-Rite Market
shops.type: Community grocery and specialty food market
shops.description: The Mission's beloved community grocery celebrated for Northern California produce, local artisan goods, craft beer, and house-made prepared foods.

shops.name: Discolandia
shops.description: A Mission District cultural landmark selling Latin vinyl records, CDs, and music merchandise, a gathering place for the neighborhood's music community.

shops.name: Precita Eyes Mural Arts Center
shops.description: The Mission's celebrated community mural arts organization offering guided mural walking tours, art supplies, and prints from the neighborhood's iconic muralist community.

shops.name: Sour Flour
shops.type: Artisan bread and community baking organization
shops.description: Mission-based artisan bread collective offering naturally leavened sourdough loaves and baking workshops rooted in community education.

shops.name: Paxton Gate
shops.description: Unique Mission shop offering taxidermy, insects, minerals, fossils, and unusual botanical specimens alongside gardening tools and gifts.

shops.name: Gravel & Gold
shops.description: Mission boutique carrying women's clothing, handmade goods, art books, and zines with an emphasis on independent and feminist makers.

shops.name: Therapy Stores
shops.type: Modern home goods and gifts boutique
shops.description: Valencia Street boutique offering a curated mix of modern home décor, quirky gifts, jewelry, and lifestyle goods.

shops.name: Baukunst Studio
shops.type: Architecture and design studio / community event space
shops.description: Bernal Heights design studio and community space housed in the historic 1924 Bank of America building on Cortland Avenue, hosting the Bernal Village Marketplace pop-ups.

artEntertainment.name: Roxie Theater
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest continuously operating cinema, founded in 1912, presenting independent, documentary, foreign, and experimental films with filmmaker Q&As and festivals year-round.

artEntertainment.name: The Portal Cinema
artEntertainment.description: A new 49-seat nonprofit arthouse cinema opening at 3293 Mission Street this fall, offering global releases, repertory screenings, and 35mm/16mm projection.

artEntertainment.description: The preserved home and studio of late conceptual artist David Ireland, open Fridays and Saturdays 12–5pm for artist-led tours exploring one of the West Coast's most important conceptual art environments.

artEntertainment.name: Galería de la Raza
artEntertainment.description: Founded in 1970, one of the Bay Area's oldest and most respected Latino arts organizations, hosting cutting-edge exhibitions, multimedia events, and community programming at its Mission location.

artEntertainment.name: Precita Eyes Murals (Balmy Alley)
artEntertainment.type: Outdoor mural art destination and tour program
artEntertainment.description: The Mission's world-famous outdoor mural corridor organized by the Precita Eyes collective since 1977, with guided walking tours departing from the Precita Eyes center on 24th Street.

artEntertainment.name: SF Community Music Center
artEntertainment.type: Community music school and performance venue
artEntertainment.description: Mission-based nonprofit offering affordable music education and presenting free and low-cost concerts in its intimate Capp Street concert hall.

artEntertainment.name: Brava Theater Center
artEntertainment.type: Women and girls theater and performance venue
artEntertainment.description: Mission District performing arts center dedicated to women and LGBTQ+ artists of color, presenting theater, dance, and multidisciplinary performances.

artEntertainment.name: Bernal Heights Outdoor Cinema
artEntertainment.description: Free outdoor film screenings of works by local filmmakers held in Bernal Heights parks and community spaces throughout the year.

artEntertainment.name: Red Poppy Art House
artEntertainment.type: Intimate concert venue and art house
artEntertainment.description: A unique Mission salon-style venue hosting intimate concerts, poetry, and cross-cultural performances in a living room setting.

gymsRecreation.name: Mission YMCA
gymsRecreation.type: Full-service community gym and recreation center
gymsRecreation.description: The Mission's full-service YMCA offering fitness equipment, group exercise classes, a pool, and youth and family programs for all fitness levels.

gymsRecreation.name: City CrossFit
gymsRecreation.description: Well-regarded CrossFit affiliate near Bernal Heights offering coached group WODs and a strong community atmosphere.

gymsRecreation.name: HAUM Studios
gymsRecreation.description: Welcoming Mission District yoga studio conveniently located near the 16th Street BART station, offering a range of yoga classes for all levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Sunporch Yoga Bernal Heights
gymsRecreation.description: Neighborhood yoga studio on Cortland Avenue offering a convenient class schedule for morning, after-work, and weekend practitioners.

gymsRecreation.name: COPAL Hot Mat
gymsRecreation.type: Hot yoga and mat fitness studio
gymsRecreation.description: Bernal Heights hot yoga and mat-based fitness studio designed to build strength, mobility, and endurance through heated classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Bernal Heights Park
gymsRecreation.type: Urban hilltop park and off-leash dog area
gymsRecreation.description: A beloved 26-acre hilltop park offering 360-degree city views, hiking trails, and one of San Francisco's largest off-leash dog areas.

gymsRecreation.name: Precita Park
gymsRecreation.description: A spacious Mission District park with open fields, a playground, and walking paths, home to the annual Precita Eyes Urban Youth Arts Festival.

gymsRecreation.name: Iron and Mettle
gymsRecreation.description: Bernal Heights–area strength and conditioning gym focused on powerlifting, Olympic lifting, and functional fitness.
